title: Module 3 Knowledge Check
description: Eight questions on learner, context, and task analysis. Unlimited attempts; best score counts.

questions.text: Interviews say learners are confident with a procedure; error logs show they fail it frequently. What should the designer do?
options: Trust the interviews; learners know themselves best
Trust the error logs and investigate why the confidence exists
Skip the analysis and start designing
questions.feedback: Triangulate, and when self-report conflicts with performance data, believe the performance data and ask why.

options: The setting where learners will use what they learned
questions.feedback: The performance context is where transfer must occur. If it does not support the new behavior, training will not produce it.

questions.text: Matching instruction to learners' self-reported learning styles (visual, auditory, kinesthetic) is well supported by research as a way to improve learning.
questions.feedback: Reviews such as Pashler et al. (2008) found no credible evidence for the matching hypothesis. Preferences may inform engagement but not the design of instruction.

questions.text: According to Gagne's taxonomy, deciding whether a scanned wristband matches the medication order is primarily which type of outcome?
questions.feedback: Making a rule-governed decision is an intellectual skill. Operating the scanner is the motor skill; choosing to scan every time is the attitude.

options: What must the learner already be able to do in order to learn this?
What does the expert think is interesting?
How long should the module be?
questions.feedback: Asking that question repeatedly produces the hierarchy of subordinate skills down to the entry-skill line.

questions.text: Procedural analysis is most likely to reveal:
options: Branch points and decisions where errors occur
questions.feedback: Branch points are where practice should concentrate and where assessment distractors come from.

questions.text: Which are appropriate ways to check a task analysis? Select all that apply.
options: Have an expert and a novice review it
Ask whether a novice could perform the goal using only what is in the analysis
Confirm it fits on one page
questions.feedback: Completeness, accuracy through observation, and expert and novice review. Page length is not a validity check.

questions.text: Where does the entry-skill line in a hierarchy come from?
questions.feedback: Entry skills are what learners already have; that is a finding of the learner analysis.
